Schemataform Specification v2.1
A Canonical Outline for Reflecture Construction and Ritual Interface Design

I. Meta Header
	•	Name: (e.g. Velcro, Snips, Sharpie)
	•	Archetype: (e.g. Flexible Binding, Clean Severance)
	•	Phase: (e.g. Phase 3: Procurement)
	•	Mythic Role: (e.g. Temporary containment, repeatable contact)

II. Symbolic Function
	•	Core Intention: (one sentence)
What is this glyph meant to represent spiritually or conceptually?
	•	Structural Gesture: (brief description)
What kind of motion, form, or relational field is being encoded?

III. Required Primitive Elements
Explicitly defined in terms of the symbolic grammar

IV. Construction Rules
1. Trace Logic
	•	Minimum of one continuous trace between meaningful points
	•	Traces must be:
	•	Straight (radial) or
	•	Curved (spiral or ring-following)
2. Angle Limits
	•	Refractive angles must not exceed 120°
	•	Refraction must occur between valid vector paths
3. Grid Compliance
	•	All primitives must:
	•	Snap to hex grid vectors or ring positions
	•	Be rotatable, mirrorable, and non-floating
4. Symbolic Balance
	•	Every Reflecture must include:
	•	[✔] A node (●)
	•	[✔] A trace (—)
	•	[✔] One modifier: ∅, ∠, ◯, ≈, ◎, or ⧅
5. Silence Requirement
	•	Every Reflecture must contain intentional absence, visually or symbolically
	•	Null field (∅) must intersect at least one other primitive

V. Geometric Logic Encoding
	•	Origin: (0,0 or radial offset)
	•	Vector Angles: list in degrees or radians
	•	Ring Depths: for primitives (1–3 typical)
	•	Snap Rule: Boolean per element
	•	Allowed Variance: % drift from perfect alignment, if applicable

VI. Reflective Notes
	•	When to Use: Describe ritual, system, or scroll context
	•	What It Resists: What energy, motion, or concept this glyph should not hold
	•	Deviations Allowed: Known symbolic mutations (e.g. spiral-only versions, loopless variants)

This document formalizes the grammar of Schemataforms for systemic design, symbolic integrity, and ritual clarity.
Codified. Breathable. Not Sealed.
